subject: language
intro: Ms. Kim here. Let's plan an 8th grade lesson on finding and evaluating credible sources.

beats.narration: The title is the question students should ask of every source.
beats.text: Can You Trust It? Evaluating Sources

beats.narration: This standard asks students to gather information from multiple sources and assess their credibility.
Four criteria give them a practical checklist.
beats.text: Students will be able to evaluate the credibility of online sources using the author, date, purpose, and evidence.

beats.narration: Most students fall for it, which makes a strong point.
beats.text: Show a convincing fake website (for example, the "Pacific Northwest Tree Octopus"). "Is this real? How can you tell?"

beats.narration: Lateral reading is what professional fact-checkers actually do.
beats.text: Model checking a source for author credentials, publication date, purpose (inform or persuade/sell), and evidence. Show lateral reading: opening a new tab to check what others say about the source.
Groups get a research question and five sources of varying quality. They rank the sources by credibility and justify each ranking.

beats.narration: This checks the application of the criteria.
beats.text: Pick one source from today. Is it credible? Use at least two criteria to explain.

outro: Fake site, model, rank, justify. Your turn to plan.
